- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility or reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts (first 5–7 days) — apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 3% in 3-day window), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days — apply downward correction of 1–3%.
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias — if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- Sentiment volatility (large swings) correlates with forecast error — when sentiment shifts sharply, model lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2% in final 5–7 days — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to last 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
